source.quote: SMSL's own page for the R100, read 2026-11-24: « R2R Soul R100 is a desktop R2R DAC that bridges the gap between classic analog warmth and modern digital performance. Powered by dual[...] » - the sentence continues past what was captured.

facts.chip: A discrete R-2R ladder, in the maker's own words « a desktop R2R DAC ». No part number: the ladder is the design.

_deliberately_thin: ONE FACT AND NO RATES. My extraction of this page caught a single sentence and cut it mid-clause at « Powered by dual »; the rest of the page was not read. What IS here - that the conversion stage is a resistor ladder - is a LEVEL 3 fact and worth a record on its own, because it changes the class and no probe would ever reveal it. The rates are a level-2 gap to fill on a second pass, not a reason to withhold the record. Recorded as thin rather than guessed at.
